findings.title: New website_name bypasses TL0 website privacy restriction
findings.body: website_name is added to attributes (line 43) but is missing from untrusted_attributes (lines 105-111). For a TL0 user viewed anonymously, the existing untrusted_attributes :website rule removes the website field, but website_name is still computed from object.user_profile.website and sent to the client. The user profile template renders model.website_name, so the hidden website host and path become visible. The TL0 spec does not catch this because its untrusted_attributes list omits :website_name and its fabricated user has no website. Add :website_name to untrusted_attributes or make the inclusion hook return false when scope.restrict_user_fields?(object), and extend the spec accordingly.

findings.title: website_name inclusion hook is never called
findings.body: The method is named include_website_name without the trailing question mark. ActiveModelSerializers looks for include_<attribute>? to decide whether to emit an attribute, so this method is dead code. website_name is therefore emitted for every serialized user, including as null when no website exists, and any inclusion logic placed here is ignored. Rename it to include_website_name? and combine it with the untrusted-field check.

findings.title: Domain comparison misclassifies unrelated hosts under multi-label public suffixes
findings.body: The elsif branch treats any two hosts with the same label count greater than two and the same suffix after the first label as the same domain. For example, with instance host foo.co.uk and user website bar.co.uk, both have three labels and suffix co.uk, so the code appends the full path from bar.co.uk even though it is a different registrable domain. The same false positive occurs for foo.github.io and bar.github.io, and similar public suffixes. This defeats the stated same-domain check and can expose a path that would otherwise be hidden. Use a public-suffix-aware registrable-domain comparison or avoid matching multi-label public suffixes this way.
